[F4 F7 F8] [NS-1]
C5: The waiting time in NS-1(iii) can be measured continuously despite ~3-minute GPS sampling, because the sampling interval (about 3 min) is not a data hole (a hole requires > 2× the normal interval and > 2 min), and the trajectory covers the whole period up to cancellation — so no G12 referral is needed on this record. [F1 F4] [NS-1]

Asks: fee_waived $5.00

The rider's version — that the driver never showed up — is contradicted by the system records (GPS position 0 m from pickup, 8 minutes stationary, platform-confirmed arrival); under the rules, the system records prevail over the rider's statement.

NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are each satisfied — arrival indicated/auto-confirmed, position within the pickup radius at that moment, and continuous waiting in radius for 8 minutes (≥ 3:01) up to the 08:51:00 cancellation — so the no-show charge stands and the correct action is no_action.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
Routing: the ride was cancelled by the driver, so the fee's validity is tested under NS-0 → NS-1 [F5]. The rider complaint that "the driver never showed up" is contradicted by the system record, which prevails over statements: the driver reached 0 m from the pickup at 08:43:00 and stayed stationary at that exact point until 08:51:00 [F2][F4][F7]. The rider advocate concedes this [F2][F4], so the only live question is whether each NS-1 element is satisfied.

NS-1(i): arrival was confirmed — platform auto-confirmation (GPS within 10 m) at 08:43:00, not a manual tap; the record is executed as written and NS-1 permits platform auto-confirmation [F6][F7]. NS-1(ii): at the moment of that confirmation the car was 0 m from the pickup point, inside the radius [F2][F7]. NS-1(iii): the driver then stayed within 200 m continuously for 8 min 0 s (480 s) up to the 08:51:00 cancellation, which meets both the 8-minute threshold carried by this case record and the policy default >3 min [F4][F7][F8]. The stay is measurable and not a GPS hole: samples run about every 3 min, a hole requires >6 min, and the trajectory covers the whole wait to cancellation, so no referral for missing evidence arises [F1][F4].

The wait was genuine and contact was attempted: four timestamped driver messages (08:43 arrival at the lobby, 08:45 car/plate SGP 4521 M, 08:49 and 08:50 prompts) and one unanswered outgoing call, with zero rider messages or replies, in a complete, fully timestamped record [F11][F12][F13][F14][F15][F16][F17]. The rider advocate argues the platform's 5-minute free period should govern the amount, but free wait time is the waiting-fee start point, not the no-show threshold, and in any event the driver waited the full 8 min 0 s the record requires [F8]. Since NS-1 is satisfied in full, no amount is refundable and the $5.00 charge on the fare record stands; under NS-1 the outcome is no_action [F9].

No NS-7 remedy arises because no waiver is owed: a voucher is the delivery form for a fee that should not have been charged, and here the fee conditions are met [F5][F9]. No account action is warranted: NS-2's flag attaches only where arrival confirmation shows the driver outside the pickup radius, and here the position was 0 m; both profiles are clean on upheld disputes and profile facts cannot decide the case anyway [F21][F22]. Refund arithmetic is therefore nil: the trace's allowed outcomes are no_action or escalate, and nothing in the record requires escalation.

SAFE-1 screen: I read all four driver chat messages, the logged call, and the rider's complaint. The messages are neutral pickup prompts and a cancellation warning ("Please let me know, otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip"), with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation from either party; the complaint is a fee grievance only [F11][F12][F13][F14][F15]. safety_concern = none.

Evidence status: sufficient. The record settles every element the ruling needs — a hole-free GPS trace covering the wait, a platform-confirmed arrival position, and a complete timestamped chat — so no evidence gap exists [F1][F3][F7][F16].

No action is being taken against your account and no complaint was filed against you. Thanks for documenting your wait; keep doing that on cancellations.

claims.assertion: The fee charged is recorded as a cancellation fee of $5.00 on a driver-cancelled trip (accepted 08:30:15, cancelled by driver 08:51:00), and NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled trip where the driver alleges rider no-show exclusively through NS-1.

NS-1(i) is nominally met: arrival was confirmed by platform auto-detection (platform_auto, GPS within 10 m) at 08:43:00 rather than by a driver button press — the record must be read as written, and the platform's clock starts only then.

NS-1(ii) is met, but on the platform's own auto-confirmation rather than a driver tap: at 08:43:00 the vehicle was 0 m from the pickup point, so it was inside the 200 m radius at the moment of arrival confirmation.

NS-1(iii) remains satisfied on the default 3-minute rule only, not on the case's own threshold: the platform's wait timer started 08:43:10 and the free period expired at 08:48:10 (5 min 0 s), yet the driver waited 8 min 0 s inside 200 m before cancelling at 08:51:00 — if any 8-minute no-show threshold applies to this record, that condition is still met, so the outcome does not turn on it.

The waiting time in NS-1(iii) can be measured continuously despite ~3-minute GPS sampling, because the sampling interval (about 3 min) is not a data hole (a hole requires > 2× the normal interval and > 2 min), and the trajectory covers the whole period up to cancellation — so no G12 referral is needed on this record.

The rider never sent a single message in reply and never answered the driver's call: 4 driver messages and 1 driver call, 0 rider messages and 0 rider calls, across a complete, fully timestamped chat record — there is no rider communication the driver could be said to be responding to.

The driver's own messages show the car was at the lobby area (notified 08:43, plate SGP 4521 M given at 08:45, a second nudge at 08:49, and a warning at 08:50 that he would cancel) — these are the only location-parked-once assertions in the file and they do not contradict the GPS fix placing the car 0 m from the pickup point.
The rider's complaint should be treated as a fee-waiver request submitted in-trip-time, and NS-7 requires any fee waiver found on review to be delivered as a $5.00 Ryde voucher, not cash.

The driver's record is clean (1 dispute, 0 upheld, no no-show history) and the rider's profile shows 4 disputes with 0 no-show disputes upheld — neither profile supports a flag_account action here, and no profile fact can decide the case alone.
